title: curriculum/majors.yaml -- the college's majors and the classes each one owns
description: The taxonomy the drill-down's top two levels are built from. Structural layer only; the cross-FILE rules (a class with no title and no coverage row, a coverage course no major claims, a course claimed twice) are enforced by ida_core.majors and tools/validate_tasks.py, because none of them can be seen from this file alone.

degree.description: The single undergraduate degree every major here sits under, as the catalog names it.

source.description: Where the list of majors was read from. Required for the same reason curriculum/slo.yaml requires one: a list of a college's majors with no cited source is an assertion, not a record.

retrieved.description: The date the catalog was read. A catalog is edited in place, so a later disagreement should be attributable to a moved goalpost rather than blamed on the transcription.

unassigned_core.description: Courses in curriculum/slo.yaml's coverage grid that no single major owns. Each needs a reason: the list is the escape hatch from the 'every coverage course is claimed' gate, and an escape hatch with no reason required is just a place to hide.

courseCode.description: Course code as the catalog prints it, e.g. 'MIS 200'. Same spelling as curriculum/slo.yaml's coverage rows -- it is the join key between the two files.

id.description: The URL segment. Written out rather than derived from `name` so that a catalog rename does not silently break every link to the major.

department.description: The department that owns the major, as the catalog names it. Not the same string as the major -- 'Information Systems, Statistics and Management Science' owns four of the eleven.

subject_codes.description: The course prefixes this major's classes carry. Recorded for the reader, not used to derive class lists: a class belongs to a major because it is listed, never because a regex matched.

display_code.description: An INFORMAL short label for a grid column header, for a major with no catalogued subject code. Not a registrar prefix: never used to match, derive or attribute a class. subject_codes stays catalog-only.

class_source.description: How far the class list got: transcribed from the catalog's course listing; only the classes this major owns in the shared business core; or nothing evidenced yet. Recorded so a short list can be shown as an incomplete transcription rather than read as a small department.

title.description: OPTIONAL, and usually omitted. When absent the title comes from curriculum/slo.yaml's coverage row for the same code, so the two files cannot disagree about a course they both name. When present it is because the course catalog is the authority on titles and the curriculum map abbreviates. A class with neither is a hard error in ida_core.majors -- it would render as a nameless column.

task_families.description: Task families whose results are ABOUT this class's own material, e.g. 'mis200-spreadsheet-formulas'. This is what makes a class's score a claim about THAT CLASS rather than about the outcomes it happens to teach. A class that lists none can never show a score, which is the correct and deliberate default: results are filed by outcome, and an outcome-filed score reaching every class that teaches the outcome would put one exam's number under a dozen courses nobody measured.
